cards.front: Why does adding "be conservative" or "only report high-confidence findings" fail to improve precision?
cards.back: The model has no shared, testable definition of those words. **Specific categorical criteria** (what to report, what to skip) give it a concrete rule to check each input against.

cards.front: Rewrite "check that comments are accurate" as an explicit criterion.
cards.back: "Flag a comment **only when the behavior it describes contradicts what the code actually does**."

cards.front: Why does one high false-positive category hurt the whole reviewer?
cards.back: Developers lose trust and start dismissing **all** findings, including accurate ones from precise categories.

cards.front: Fastest way to restore developer trust when one review category is noisy?
cards.back: **Temporarily disable that category** while you rewrite its criteria; keep the precise categories running.

cards.front: How do you get consistent severity labels?
cards.back: Define each severity level explicitly and attach a **concrete code example** to each level.

cards.front: The prompt "golden rule"
cards.back: Show the prompt to a colleague with little context. If they'd be confused, Claude will be too.

cards.front: Why explain the reason behind an instruction?
cards.back: Claude **generalizes from the reason**, so it also avoids related problems you didn't list.

cards.front: Where should long documents (20k+ tokens) go in a prompt?
cards.back: **At the top**, with the query/instructions at the **end**. Anthropic's tests showed up to 30% better answers. Asking for relevant quotes first also helps.

cards.front: Does prefill work on Claude 4.6+ models?
cards.back: No. A request ending with an assistant message returns **HTTP 400**. Use structured outputs, strict tool use, or direct instructions.

cards.front: When is few-shot prompting the right next step?
cards.back: When **detailed instructions alone still produce inconsistent** format or judgment.

cards.front: How many few-shot examples for ambiguous cases?
cards.back: Exam guide: **2-4 targeted examples**. Anthropic docs: 3-5. A few well-chosen, diverse examples, not dozens.

cards.front: What should a few-shot example for an ambiguous case include?
cards.back: The input, the chosen action, and **why it beat the plausible alternatives**, so the model generalizes the principle to new cases.

cards.front: How do few-shot examples reduce false positives?
cards.back: Include examples of **acceptable patterns that are not findings** next to genuine issues.

cards.front: An extractor returns null for required fields only for some document layouts. Fix?
cards.back: Add **few-shot examples covering those layouts** (e.g. inline citations vs bibliography).

cards.front: Most reliable way to get schema-compliant structured output?
cards.back: **Tool use with a JSON schema** (input_schema); read data from the `tool_use` block's `input`. It eliminates JSON syntax errors.

cards.front: tool_choice `auto` vs `any` vs forced
cards.back: `auto`: may reply with text. `any`: must call **some** tool. `{"type":"tool","name":"X"}`: must call **tool X**.

cards.front: Several extraction schemas exist and the document type is unknown. Which tool_choice?
cards.back: `{"type": "any"}`: guarantees a tool call while letting Claude pick the matching schema.

cards.front: How do you make sure extract_metadata runs before enrichment steps?
cards.back: Force it: `tool_choice: {"type": "tool", "name": "extract_metadata"}`, then continue in follow-up turns.

cards.front: What does a strict JSON schema NOT prevent?
cards.back: **Semantic errors**: line items that don't sum to the total, values in the wrong field, wrong-but-valid values.

cards.front: Current-docs caveat on tool_choice any/forced
cards.back: Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 return 400 for `any`/`tool`; docs recommend `auto` + `strict: true` or `output_config.format`. The exam tests the classic concepts.

cards.front: Name the two grammar-constrained structured output features in current docs.
cards.back: `strict: true` on a tool definition, and JSON outputs via `output_config.format` (the old `output_format` is deprecated). JSON outputs (`output_config.format`) can't be combined with citations (400).

cards.front: Why make a schema field nullable?
cards.back: If the source may not contain the value, a required non-nullable field pushes the model to **fabricate** one. Nullable lets it return `null`.

cards.front: Pattern for a category list that will grow
cards.back: Enum with **"other"** plus a **detail string** field; add **"unclear"** for ambiguous inputs.

cards.front: Dates come out in mixed formats despite a strict schema. Fix?
cards.back: Add **normalization rules** to the prompt (e.g. ISO 8601) alongside the schema.

cards.front: What goes in an effective retry request?
cards.back: The **original document**, the **failed extraction**, and the **specific validation errors**.

cards.front: When will retrying an extraction NOT help?
cards.back: When the information is **absent from the source** (e.g. only in an external document not provided). Return null / escalate instead.

cards.front: Syntax errors vs semantic errors after adopting tool use
cards.back: Syntax errors are **eliminated** by the schema. Semantic errors (sums, wrong fields) need **application validation**.

cards.front: Purpose of calculated_total next to stated_total?
cards.back: Lets code detect discrepancies between the printed total and the sum of extracted line items.

cards.front: Purpose of a detected_pattern field on review findings?
cards.back: Lets you analyze **which code patterns developers dismiss**, so you can fix or disable those criteria.

cards.front: Message Batches API: cost, window, SLA
cards.back: **50%** cheaper, up to **24 hours** processing, **no latency SLA** (most finish within about an hour, not guaranteed).

cards.front: How are batch results matched to requests?
cards.back: By **`custom_id`**. Results can come back in any order.

cards.front: Batch or sync: blocking pre-merge check vs overnight tech-debt report?
cards.back: Pre-merge: **synchronous** (someone is waiting). Overnight report: **batch**.

cards.front: Can a batch request run a multi-turn tool loop?
cards.back: No, not with your own (client) tools: you can't execute them mid-request and feed results back within one batch item. Multi-step agent loops need sync calls or separate batch rounds. (Anthropic's server tools like web search do run their loop inside a batch.)

cards.front: Batch SLA math: 30-hour SLA with 24-hour processing
cards.back: Submission interval + 24 h must be <= 30 h, so submit at least every **6 hours** (the guide's 4-hour windows give margin).

cards.front: Some batch items failed because documents exceeded the context. What now?
cards.back: Resubmit **only the failed custom_ids**, after **chunking** those documents. Don't re-run the whole batch.

cards.front: Why is self-review in the same session weak?
cards.back: The model keeps its **generation reasoning** in context and is less likely to question its own decisions.

cards.front: Better than self-review or extended thinking for catching subtle issues?
cards.back: An **independent Claude instance** that sees the artifact and criteria but not the generator's reasoning.

cards.front: Fix for a 14-file single-pass review with uneven depth and contradictions
cards.back: **Per-file passes** for local issues + a separate **integration pass** for cross-file data flow (attention dilution).

cards.front: Why is "keep findings 2 of 3 runs agree on" a bad review fix?
cards.back: It **suppresses real bugs** that are only caught intermittently.

cards.front: What is per-finding self-reported confidence good for?
cards.back: **Routing** review effort (auto-post vs human check), not replacing explicit criteria.
